extracted.intended_audience: Authors and teams preparing Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions (review authors, editors, and methodologists)
extracted.subtask_description: High-level methodological and procedural guidance for planning and initiating a Cochrane systematic review of intervention effects, including protocol development, team composition, search and synthesis planning, and quality assurance. Intended to ensure transparent, reproducible, and low-bias review conduct and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a systematic review
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic review attempts to collate all the empirical evidence that fits pre-specified eligibility criteria in order to answer a specific research question; it uses explicit, systematic methods selected to minimize bias and provide more reliable findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews provide up-to-date summaries for decision makers, aim to minimize bias (analogous to methods in primary studies), and should be undertaken before commissioning new primary research to avoid unnecessary duplication and to identify gaps. They should give balanced summaries of benefits and harms and indicate certainty in findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation of the review question (use PICO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting the research question right is critical; for questions about effects of interventions the PICO approach (Population, Intervention, Comparison(s), Outcome) is usually used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the question addresses an important issue for expected users. Consider additional questions (implementation, economic, equity, patient experience). Question formulation should be informed by a wide range of perspectives and stakeholders (see Chapter 2). The review question should determine methods, not vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition: include topic and methodological expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews should be undertaken by a team; Cochrane will not publish a review proposed to be undertaken by a single person. Teams must include expertise in the topic area and in systematic review methodology, including statistical expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic expertise should not be overly narrow and multiple disciplinary perspectives are valuable. Methodological expertise helps avoid bias from prior knowledge. First-time authors are encouraged to work with experienced colleagues and attend training. Team membership supports independent duplicate tasks (selection, data extraction, rating certainty) to minimize errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest management
rubrics_metrics.description: A Cochrane review should represent an independent assessment of the evidence; financial and non-financial conflicts of interest must be carefully managed. Funding of Cochrane reviews by commercial organizations with an interest in the outcome is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the Conflict of Interest Policy, make complete declarations of interest before registration and refresh these annually until publication and just prior to publication. Update declarations when circumstances change. Some situations (employment, patents, other financial support) may prevent people joining an author team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involving consumers and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: People who might make or be affected by decisions (consumers, policy makers, funders, healthcare professionals) should be involved in important decisions about the review to increase relevance and uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map potential stakeholders and balance seniority, credibility and diversity. Consider input from resource-poor regions. Consumers (patients, carers, service users, public) should be involved; Cochrane's Statement of Principles promotes partnership from planning through dissemination. Methods for involvement include surveys, workshops, focus groups, advisory groups; provide support (reimbursement, training), clear expectations, terms of reference, and ensure advisory group membership reflects review breadth and includes vulnerable/marginalized people where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work methods with consumers and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide who to involve, how to support involvement, and choose appropriate methods given resources; advisory groups can be used to involve a wider range of perspectives without making everyone co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate advisory input to inform key review decisions and maintain input throughout the review. Use templates (job descriptions, terms of reference) and resources (INVOLVE, Patient and public page) to support engagement. Expect some participants to be authors and others to be advisory contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of reliability and auditability
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews aim to be an accurate, auditable representation of current knowledge because decisions (including legal/regulatory) are made from review findings; reviews must be correct and seen to be correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed evidence-based methods, document procedures to aid auditability, and include information to allow legal examination. Reliability requires planned methods to identify and account for bias in included studies and in review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MECIR expectations for conduct and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane's Methodological Expectations for Conduct and Reporting (MECIR) and Plain Language Expectations (PLEACS) describe desirable attributes of Cochrane reviews and their summaries; items are classed as 'mandatory' or 'highly desirable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which expectations are relevant at specific stages. Mandatory items are expected to be applied and failure to implement may justify not publishing in CDSR unless an appropriate justification is provided. Highly desirable items should generally be implemented though exceptions may be reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol development and pre-specification of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and judgements should be established and documented in advance in a protocol to minimize bias arising from knowledge of study findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and registration (all Cochrane Protocols published in CDSR; register on PROSPERO) promote transparency, reduce duplication and allow peer review of methods. The protocol should define eligibility criteria, planned analyses (including heterogeneity investigations), methods for interpreting results and factors affecting confidence in estimates. Consult all Handbook chapters when drafting protocols. Some exceptions (prospectively planned meta-analysis, living reviews) exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid post hoc changes to protocol based on results
rubrics_metrics.description: While changes to a protocol can be necessary, changes should not be made based on their effect on results; post hoc decisions influenced by known results are highly susceptible to bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes are necessary, they must be transparently declared. Treat protocol changes similarly to trial protocol changes—document rationale and timing; do not exclude studies or change analyses because of their impact on outcomes unless there are reasonable grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: C19: Planning the search (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance methods to identify studies. Design searches to capture as many studies as possible that meet the eligibility criteria, ensuring relevant time periods and sources are covered and not restricted by language or publication status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches should be motivated by eligibility criteria. Avoid restricting by publication status or language to prevent publication/language bias. Removing language restrictions in English-language databases is not a substitute for searching non-English databases/journals. Consider unpublished sources to reduce reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: C20: Planning assessment of risk of bias in included studies (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance methods to assess risk of bias, including the tool(s) to be used, how they will be implemented, and the criteria for assigning low/unclear/high risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefining methods and criteria is important because analysis/interpretation may be affected by these judgements. For randomized trials, use of the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool is Mandatory; reviews can simply refer to Handbook definitions for low/unclear/high. Specify implementation details (who assesses, whether assessments are independent, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: C21: Planning the synthesis of results (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance methods to synthesize results, including whether quantitative synthesis is planned, how heterogeneity will be assessed, choice of effect measure (odds ratio, risk ratio, risk difference, etc.), and meta-analysis methods (inverse variance, Mantel–Haenszel; fixed-effect or random-effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefining statistical synthesis methods is important because analysis/interpretation can be affected by analysis choices. Specify effect measures and meta-analysis models in the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: C22: Planning sub-group analyses (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefine potential effect modifiers for subgroup analyses at the protocol stage; restrict their number and provide rationale for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specification reduces the risk that many undirected subgroup analyses will lead to spurious explanations of heterogeneity. Limit subgroup analyses to those with credible rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: C23: Planning GRADE assessment and Summary of Findings table (Mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance methods to assess certainty of the body of evidence (GRADE) and summarise findings. Pre-specify choice of important outcomes to include in 'Summary of findings' tables (typically up to seven).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefining outcomes guards against selective presentation. Include essential decision-making outcomes, avoid surrogate/interim outcomes, and do not choose outcomes based on anticipated or observed magnitude of effect or because they are likely to have been addressed in the included studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefine methods to examine biases within included studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan methods to examine issues that create bias within included studies (e.g., methods of allocation, awareness of group assignment, and data collection/analysis/reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify tools and procedures to assess these biases in the protocol (see C20). Consider how study-level biases will be accounted for when interpreting the body of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational data management and quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of inclusion decisions, data collection, data transformations/adjustments, and other review decisions to create a secure retrievable audit trail and ensure replicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use review management software (e.g., Covidence, EPPI-Reviewer) to assist data management and standardized records. Record independent assessments of inclusion, risk of bias and data extraction. Quality assurance is essential despite cost in author time because even experienced reviewers make mistakes. Good data management facilitates updates and future automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping to facilitate updates and automation
rubrics_metrics.description: All review data — including initial decisions about study eligibility — have value beyond the individual review and should be preserved to support efficient updates and potential semi-automation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain data in formats and repositories that enable reuse, support reproducibility, and allow future machine-learning assisted updates (see Chapters 4 and 22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol should define eligibility criteria and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol sets out the review context and should define eligibility criteria for participants, comparators, outcomes, study designs, and any logic model or conceptualisation of how the intervention might work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility criteria may be shaped by a logic model; define these in advance to prevent selection based on known results. Use the protocol to plan analyses, grouping for synthesis, and handling of different study types (e.g., network meta-analysis considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use independent, duplicate processes for key review tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks such as study selection for eligibility, data extraction and rating certainty should be performed by at least two people independently to minimise errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teamworking spreads effort and reduces errors; specify who does duplicate work and how disagreements will be resolved. Document these procedures in the protocol and maintain records of independent assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure search breadth and inclusion of all eligible study types
rubrics_metrics.description: When planning searches, consider all types of eligible studies (study designs) and ensure searches capture relevant time periods and sources without inappropriate restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivate search strategies by eligibility criteria. If searches are restricted by publication status or language, there is risk of publication/language bias. Include grey literature and unpublished sources where needed to reduce reporting bias (see Dwan et al. 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for pre-specifying analyses and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The review question should determine the methods and outcomes pre-specified in the protocol; pre-specification reduces bias and selective reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define analyses (including heterogeneity investigations), choice of effect measures and primary/important outcomes before seeing study results. Limit number of outcomes in Summary of Findings to those essential for decisions (typically up to seven).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public access to protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Make protocols accessible through publication and registration to promote accountability, reduce duplication and research waste, and enable peer review of planned methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish Cochrane Protocols in CDSR and register reviews on PROSPERO. Transparently declare and justify changes to protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to consult full Handbook when drafting protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: All Handbook chapters, including later-stage procedures, should be consulted when preparing the protocol so that methods are consistent and comprehensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to relevant chapters for detailed methods (searching, risk of bias tools, statistical methods, GRADE, reporting) and for Cochrane-specific expectations (MECIR, PLEACS).
